rationale: Y's findings overlap meaningfully with ground truth — it independently surfaces the same WebSocket/HTTP streaming-speed asymmetry the top human inline comment flagged (via docs/serving/speech_api.md vs the fixed audio.py/serving_speech.py behavior), and validates the native-speed fix state, while backing every claim with verbatim evidence quotes and line numbers that are hard to fabricate. X produces a thorough, well-argued review but on an almost entirely disjoint set of concerns (checkpoint bias init, payload CONCAT semantics, snapshot copying, prefix-caching errors) that don't match any ground-truth comment, and its claims read as plausible but less verifiably grounded (speculative phrasing, no verbatim evidence). Both are reasonably actionable with concrete file/line targets, giving X a slight edge there, but Y wins clearly on recall and precision.
